The market is extremely volatile under the surface:

The difference between individual stock volatility in the S&P 500 and the S&P 500 Volatility Index, $VIX, is up to a record 34 points.

This gap has surged +19 points, or +127%, since March.

Over this period, the individual stock volatility index has risen +9 points, to 49 points, the highest since March 2025.

At the same time, $VIX has declined -16 points, to 15 points, the lowest since mid-January.

In other words, the calm in the broader market is hiding unusually high stress across individual stocks.

This comes as the concentration in mega-cap tech continues to keep index volatility artificially low.

Single stocks are trading as if a correction has already occurred.

Japan's bond market is seeing historic volatility.

The 10Y Japanese government bond yield dropped -16 basis points on Friday, to 2.71%, the largest daily decline since April 2025.

This follows a rise to 2.90% on Thursday, the first time the 10Y JGB yield reached that level in 30 years.

At the same time, the 30Y JGB yield fell -13 basis points, to 3.87%, the largest daily drop since January 21st.

This came after Japan's Finance Minister said the government wants to encourage pension funds, including the $1.8 trillion Government Pension Investment Fund, to increase investment in domestic assets.

If this materializes, Japan's largest pension fund could eventually shift allocation away from overseas securities and toward JGBs, easing pressure on the domestic debt market.

The move could also support the Yen by reducing capital outflows from Japan.

Japan’s bond and currency markets are set to remain highly volatile.

Out of 12 months in a year, cyclical nature of the markets offer 2-3 months of strong winners (Type 1 and Type 2 breakouts) rest of the time Type 1s are spread out with more Type 3 and Type 4s. 

It is these strong months and the ability to capture strong breakouts gives you the edge in trading breakout strategies.

There is no perfect and bullet proof stop-loss strategy. 

A logical place is always below the pattern boundary after the breakout. 

You can place your stop-loss below the pattern boundary and still above the Last Full Day low, and have a much higher reward/risk but you will get stopped out more often, resulting in a lower win%.

You can enter with stop-limit orders during the day without waiting for the daily close and place your stop-loss between the boundary and the Last Full Day low and have even a higher reward/risk with probably lower win%

See which one you are comfortable with. This the part your personality and risk tolerance will be involved. You will get to know what works better for you.

If price does a hard re-test, a tight stop-loss below the pattern boundary will get triggered. You can say, I am not interested in a re-entry and go shop elsewhere, or if you really need to be invested in that stock, you start looking for re-entry levels as long as the pattern is not negated.

Here is a video on re-entry condition.

You can get stopped out of a pattern breakout trade, but the pattern can still be valid. If the pattern is still valid, it can offer a re-entry signal incase you got stopped out.

At what level we say that the pattern is not valid anymore? At the red line, the pattern negation level. It is not a stop-loss.

Trend and consolidation. The 5 month-long ascending triangle with the horizontal upper boundary is the consolidation.

Broken out on the upside is the beginning of a new trend period. 

By acting on the breakout and placing stops below the pattern boundary, you are limiting your risk but having unlimited upside potential. This is asymmetric trading.

Expand your horizon. When you are buying the breakout from a well-defined consolidation, you are actually participating in the next trend period. Trends can extend. You are not bound by the price target. 

Make the pattern boundary your uncle point once the move takes off... Capture the trend.
View this example with the text below. https://t.co/XMpQnhZYwX

If I wait for a breakout confirmation, I will be late and miss the upside potential...

This is the FOMO of breakouts signals.

FOMO is destructive in all situations.

A breakout once confirmed starts a new trend period. It doesn't mean that it is capped with the price target. Price targets are guidelines only.
Even though an ascending triangle has a bullish bias, it is just a bias. It should not be used as a predictive pattern to build bullish case until a clear breakout confirms the pattern.

Diamonds are rare and more prone to morphing. I know that the diamond interpretation has become widespread on X. And it is being used as a predictive pattern to confirm bearish narratives.

I'm thinking we have a neutral chart pattern setup here with volatility dropping above the year-long average and a breakout higher will be a signal in the direction of the overall trend.
